transcript.statement: Sustainability is crucial for the library management system. GRN-01 ensures energy-efficient servers, reducing overall energy consumption. GRN-02 tracks energy usage, promoting accountability in operations. GRN-03 enables digital notifications, minimizing paper waste. GRN-04 allows members to assess each book's carbon footprint, fostering awareness. GRN-05 ensures proper disposal of damaged books, reinforcing responsibility. GRN-06 tracks energy savings, justifying the shift to digital. GRN-07 prioritizes e-books, significantly lowering physical resource consumption. These requirements promote a sustainable library environment.

transcript.statement: Trustworthiness is essential for the library management system to ensure data protection and security. TRU-01 guarantees that only authenticated members can borrow or return books, while TRU-02 ensures all transactions are logged for auditability. TRU-03 enforces data encryption for personal information, safeguarding privacy. TRU-04 implements role-based access control, enhancing security for both members and librarians. TRU-05 provides a secure mechanism for reporting overdue books, and TRU-06 allows members to update their personal information safely. TRU-07 ensures strong password policies to prevent unauthorized access. These requirements collectively enhance the system's integrity and user trust.

conflicts_raised.description: The requirement for digital notifications (GRN-03) may conflict with member privacy if personal information is not adequately protected as outlined in TRU-03.

transcript.statement: Performance efficiency is critical for the library management system to ensure fast, reliable, and responsive operations. EFF-01 guarantees that book searches are responsive under 2 seconds, enhancing user experience. EFF-02 allows for 10 simultaneous borrow operations, optimizing resource utilization. EFF-03 ensures real-time tracking of book availability, which is essential for user satisfaction. EFF-04 mandates quick processing of returns to maintain a high throughput. EFF-05 emphasizes timely overdue notifications for accountability. EFF-06 ensures efficient book management by librarians, and EFF-07 maintains system uptime, critical for consistent access. These requirements collectively ensure the system runs efficiently and meets user expectations.

conflicts_raised.description: The energy efficiency measures in GRN-01 may limit the resources available for achieving the performance metrics outlined in EFF-01 and EFF-04.

transcript.statement: Ethical compliance is vital for the library management system. RES-01 ensures data protection by implementing encryption, safeguarding member information. RES-02 promotes fairness by providing an accessible interface for all users, including those with disabilities. RES-03 logs all user actions to ensure accountability in library operations. RES-04 enforces borrowing policies to maintain fairness and prevent abuse. RES-05 notifies members of overdue books, promoting responsibility. RES-06 enables member feedback, enhancing service quality. RES-07 ensures transparency through annual usage reports, fostering trust and accountability. These requirements are crucial for ethical and responsible library management.

transcript.statement: Safety and reliability are paramount in the library management system. SAF-01 ensures that members do not exceed borrowing limits, preventing resource strain. SAF-02 provides timely overdue notifications, reducing the chance of lost books. SAF-03 maintains real-time inventory, preventing double borrowing and ensuring accurate tracking. SAF-04 establishes a backup mechanism to recover transaction data, enhancing fault tolerance. SAF-05 allows librarians to manage borrowing privileges, ensuring accountability. SAF-06 protects the borrowing system through user authentication. SAF-07 logs all transactions for auditing, reinforcing reliability. Together, these requirements create a safe and dependable environment for library operations.

requirements.text: The system shall ensure that only authenticated members can borrow or return books.
The system shall log all transactions for auditability and accountability purposes.
The system shall implement data encryption for all member personal information stored to ensure data protection.
The system shall enforce a maximum of 5 books per member to maintain fair borrowing practices.
The system shall provide secure digital notifications for overdue books to promote responsibility.
The system shall maintain real-time inventory status of all books for accurate tracking.
The system shall explore energy-efficient methods for real-time inventory tracking.
The system shall provide an accessible interface for all users to promote fairness and inclusivity.
The system shall maintain an uptime of 99.5% to ensure consistent availability for users.
